newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson names new CEO and boardmembers.
newsitem.headline: Molson names new CEO and boardmembers.

text.p: In a surprise move on Friday Molson Cos. Ltd., a joint partner of Canada's biggest beermaker, said it replaced its chief executive officer and added three new members to its board or directors.
Moslon said it named James Arnett president and chief executive officer to replace Norman Seagram who resigned after holding the reins of the 200-year-old company for only nine months.

"The story is that the board (of Directors) of this company has made a decision, unanimously I might add, that we ought to have a more modern form of corporate governance," Arnett said in a telepnone interview.

The company also reconsituted an executive committee consisting of board member Ian Molson as executive committee chairman, Molson Cos. Chairman Eric Molson, Arnett and Matthew Barrett, Chairman of the Bank of Montreal.
"That's going to be an executive committee with which I as CEO am going to work closely," Arnett said.
Arnett said the corporate changes would not change Molson's commitment to focusing on the brewing part of its business, which Seagram announced when he was made chief executive in September 1996.

"That is still our focus," Arnett said. "The way we look at it now is that this governance structure is going to help us deal with the rather complex issues that have to be dealt with to get us from where we are now to being that operating brewing company."
Molson Breweries is 40 percent owned by the Molson Cos. Ltd., 40 percent by Foster's Brewing Group Ltd. and 20 percent by Philip Morris Cos. Inc. brewing unit Miller Brewing Co.

Arnett admitted that Molson might be considering buying back Miller's 20 percent stake in the wake of a recent settlement of a dispute between Molson Cos. and Adolph Coors Co., which requires Miller's approval.
"That is certainly a possibility and if the conditions are right that can happen," Arnett said.
Molson has sold off interest in some of its assets this year in an attempt to distance the company from its past status as a diversified holding company.

"These changes will enable management and the board of directors to improve the way that we govern and manage The Molson Companies," said Eric Molson. "Our new chief executive officer, Jim Arnett, will work closely with the executive committee and the board to achieve our strategic priority - operating brewing status."
